question: P sells an article which costs him Rs. 1,200 to Q at a profit of 15%. Q then sells it to R for Rs.1,449 What is the profit percentage of Q?
solution:
Given:

P sells an article that costs him Rs. 1,200 to Q at a profit of 15%.

Q then sells it to R for Rs.1,449.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

The cost price of the article incurred to Q = 1200 + 1200 × 15% = Rs. 1380

Let the profit percentage of Q be M%.

According to the concept,

1380 + 1380 × M% = 1449

⇒ 1380 × M% = 1449 - 1380

⇒ M% = 69/1380

⇒ M% = 0.05

⇒ M = 5

∴ The profit percentage of Q is 5%.

Now, profit% of Q = {{1449 - 1380} over 1380} times 100\% = 5%

∴ The profit percentage of Q is 5%.
